_note: Voice configuration for the self-hosted TTS subsystem. 'default_engine' is what generate_voiceover.py and the animation pipeline use when no --engine is given. Aliases map the pipeline's Edge-style voice names (and common shorthand) to native engine voice ids. The 'catalog' section documents every selectable Kokoro voice with its style and best-fit use; it is informational for humans and the benchmark report, not a runtime whitelist. Do not add voices here that the engine on this machine cannot actually speak — verify with `python3 universal_toolbook/generate_voiceover.py --voices`.

selection._note: Voice selection policy. 'default_voice' is used for new projects and whenever no project/channel voice is set. 'automatic' describes how the pipeline picks a voice when a project does not name one: it is ALWAYS a single deterministic lookup (default_voice), never random and never per-scene — one run, one voice, from start to finish. Per-scene or per-channel switching is only possible by explicitly setting the voice in the project config. If a requested voice is not installed, the engine reports which file is missing and falls back to the default voice of that engine (documented, never silent).

kokoro._note: Kokoro-82M int8 ONNX via the kokoro-onnx package. Weights are in runtime/cache/tts/ (downloaded by setup_tts.py). voice_files are merged in order: the first file's names win on collisions, later files add new names; the v1.0 re-recordings of the 11 shared names are registered with a _v1 suffix by the provider. 24000 Hz output. No native word timings on this export — the subsystem applies the syllable-proportional + energy-refined fallback.

catalog._note: Style notes are community descriptions from the Kokoro voice catalog, NOT verified quality claims — the benchmark report (docs/production/TTS_VOICE_COMPARISON.md) has the measurements and samples. 'set': v019 = v0.19 set (plain name), v1 = v1.0 re-recording (plain name), v1_only = v1.0-only voice (plain name), v019_v1_variant = v1.0 re-recording reachable as <name>_v1 because the plain name is the v0.19 recording.

am_michael.note: PRIMARY default for new projects and automatic selection

af.note: the unnamed base voice of the v0.19 set

bm_atten_inno.style: British, added by the 'inno' community set (community-described)

am_michael_v1.style: v1.0 re-recording of Michael (A/B against am_michael)

af_bella_v1.style: v1.0 re-recording of Bella (A/B against af_bella)

piper._note: Piper (piper1-gpl) medium-quality voices from the 007-Akira/Project-Rocky GitHub mirror (the repo's standard offline fallback). Voices live in ~/.cache/piper_voices. 22050 Hz output. Native phoneme-level alignments are available. FALLBACK ONLY by policy — ryan-medium's natural pace is noticeably faster than the Kokoro defaults (see TTS_VOICE_COMPARISON.md); Piper never takes over from Kokoro while Kokoro is available, and its speaking rate is not slowed to imitate Kokoro (that degrades the voice). Supported rate control: speed (synthesis rate scale); length_scale is the inverse and is not used.

edge._note: Microsoft Edge TTS. Kept ONLY as a fallback for machines where the sandbox network allows speech.platform.bing.com. Proprietary cloud service — not free-tier guaranteed, not self-hosted. In this Arena sandbox it is unreachable and synthesis fails per line (the pipeline then falls through to the offline engines).

processing._note: Applied by generate_voiceover.py (processing on by default) and process_audio.py. Chain: resample -> peak pre-pass -> RMS loudness normalize -> soft peak limit. The RMS target (-16 dBFS, matching the repo's narration QC band -16..-19 dBFS) is the PRIMARY loudness control so every segment sits at the same level; the peak pre-pass only LOWERS peaks above -1 dBFS (it never amplifies) and the soft limit at -0.5 dBFS is the safety net. No compression. Originals are always kept alongside processed files.

segmentation._note: How text is split into segments. Paragraph break = blank line. Sentences end at . ! ? … — ; clauses at , ; : and ( ). max_segment_chars guards engine chunk limits by splitting long sentences at clause boundaries.
